 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. As the Milwaukee Brewers prepare to take the field for Game 1 of the World Series, there is a familiar face many fans will be looking for before the first pitch.
 She is not a player, coach or member of the team's front office. But for Brewers fans who regularly watch games on television, she has become almost as recognizable as some of the people wearing the uniform.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Her name is Amy Williams, better known to baseball fans as Front Row Amy, and her dedication to the Brewers has made her one of the team's most recognizable super fans.
 With Milwaukee back in the World Series for the first time since 1982, Williams will have an opportunity to watch the team she loves compete for its first championship in franchise history. Here is her background.

 Amy Williams, or Front row Amy during the Milwaukee Brewers National League Championship Series game against the Los Angeles Dodgers at American Family Field on Oct 12, 2026. Mark Hoffman / Milwaukee Journal Sentinel
 Who Is Front Row Amy? The Legendary Brewers Fan
 Front Row Amy is a longtime Brewers fan and season-ticket holder who has become famous for sitting directly behind home plate at American Family Field.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Williams lives in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, and regularly makes the drive to Milwaukee to watch her team play. She typically attends around 40 regular-season games each year, although she attended 35 during the 2026 season. She also plans to attend the Brewers' home postseason games.
 Her famous seat is in Section 117, Row 1, Seat 5. She began sitting in the front row in 2011 after spending the previous couple of seasons in the fourth row of the same section.
 Her location makes her easy to spot during television broadcasts, particularly when the cameras turn toward home plate. Over time, fans began recognizing her as a regular presence at Brewers games, and the nickname Front Row Amy stuck.
 But her connection to baseball goes beyond having a good seat.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Williams is known for keeping score by hand throughout games, carefully following pitches and recording what happens on the field. She has explained that pitching is her favorite part of baseball, and her attention to detail is a big part of what makes attending games so enjoyable for her.
 How Amy Williams Became a Brewers Fan
 One of the more interesting parts of Williams' story is that she was not always a devoted baseball fan.
 According to an interview with the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel , she became interested in the Brewers in 2007 while recovering from surgery at home. She started watching games on television and quickly became hooked.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement She attended her first game at the team's former home, Miller Park, with her husband. The experience helped turn a growing interest into a lasting passion.
 By 2008, she had purchased season tickets, and she eventually settled into the seat that made her recognizable to baseball fans throughout the country.
 Her dedication has continued for nearly two decades. Williams has said she probably has not missed a Brewers game, whether in person, on television or on the radio, since May 2007.
 That is a remarkable commitment for any fan, especially one who lives more than an hour away from the ballpark.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In an interview with the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel , Williams summed up her connection to the team in a way many sports fans can understand.
 "I'm just a normal person. I'm just a normal fan like anyone else who really, really loves the Brewers," she said.
 Oct 14, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang (2) slides to third base against the Los Angeles Dodgers during the eighth inning in game three of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images
 Front Row Amy and the Brewers' World Series Run
 Williams has had a front-row view of some memorable moments in Brewers history, but the team's 2026 postseason has given her another reason to be excited.
 She was at American Family Field for Game 2 of the National League Division Series against the San Diego Padres on October 4. The game happened to fall on her 58th birthday, and Milwaukee delivered a dramatic ninth-inning comeback victory.
 Speaking to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel , Williams described the experience as something she would not soon forget.
 "That was amazing. I kind of forgot it was my birthday because I was so focused on the game," she said. "And, that game − I've never felt like that. That was crazy."
 The Brewers went on to sweep the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, earning their first World Series appearance since 1982.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Now, as Milwaukee prepares to face the Tampa Bay Rays in the Fall Classic, Williams is once again part of the scene surrounding the team.
